title: Don’t buy the lake house until you read page two

 Don’t Buy the Lake House Until You Read Page Two
Hi Sara,
You get an offer for $3 million.
You do the math, picture the lake house, maybe even start browsing Zillow.
But here’s the thing:
That top-line number? It’s not always what hits your bank account.
One of the biggest traps in dealmaking is comparing LOIs like real estate listings: price first, details later. And it’s understandable. A big, bold number is exciting.
But in these deals, the details are the price.
Here’s what sellers often miss:
A “normalized working capital” clause can quietly slice hundreds of thousands off your cash at close.

Rollover equity might sound great, but you need to know what company it’s actually in, and how it’s valued (and how it’s forfeited-yikes!).

So two offers that look the same on paper might leave you with radically different outcomes - and radically different bank account balances.
That’s why I spend so much time helping clients understand what they’re actually agreeing to, not just what looks good on page one.
If you want to see how I break down LOIs and deal terms in plain English, check out the DealMakers YouTube channel.
To smarter exits (and real lake house money),
Sara Sharp
Deal Attorney & Founder, Deal Academy
